transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-03-16 14:30 PT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Ivy Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Sam Rivera (Redwood Support) — Leah Ortiz (CedarPoint Head of AI), Tom Bowers (Infra Eng), Priya Anand (Product)

Summary/Topics (auto-gen may be fuzzy): rapid prototype, TTFT, hosted api credits, privacy/VPC, SOC2/KMS, perf benchmarks, next steps

00:00:12 Ivy Chen: Alright everyone, thanks for hopping on, I think we have about 45 minutes, quick intros?
00:00:18 Leah Ortiz: Hi I'm Leah, Head of AI at CedarPoint Retail. We're exploring a small prototype to add conversational product helper into our mobile app, mainly to validate latency and relevance on our catalog.
00:00:30 Tom Bowers: Tom here, infra. I'll be looking at networking/security and how this will fit with our VPC policies.
00:00:35 Priya Anand: Priya, product. Focused on success criteria and timeline.
00:00:40 Ivy Chen: Cool — I'm Ivy, AE at Redwood. Marcus is our SE, he'll talk infra/perf. Sam is here for support questions. Quick agenda: understand current stack, constraints, decide a TTFT path (self-serve hosted credits vs dedicated), define pilot success metrics and next steps.

00:01:05 Marcus Patel: Hey all. Quick note, we'll cover sample throughput, expected RPS, latency SLOs, and what we'd need to run a small benchmark.

00:01:22 Leah Ortiz: Our baseline: current prototype uses an in-house retrieval model + light LM reranker. Average user session 2-3 queries, target 95th percentile latency under 600ms for generation end-to-end. Data residency in US only, and we need audit logs for early stage.
00:01:45 Ivy Chen: That's helpful. For time-to-first-token we usually recommend starting on Redwood Hosted API with free trial credits. It gets you to first call in under an hour for many teams — sign-up, API key, sample prompts. Does that align with your security posture?
00:02:00 Tom Bowers: Potentially. But we need to check KMS integration and audit logs. We also have a compliance checklist — SOC2 + some internal policy.
00:02:09 Ivy Chen: Right. Hosted supports SOC2 controls from our side, audit logs, and we can provide a security pack. For KMS customer-managed keys, that's typically available on Redwood Private; for Hosted we have encryption at rest with our managed keys. We'll share the SOC2 whitepaper and the KMS options.
00:02:30 Leah Ortiz: Okay, can you also clarify data retention? We can't retain PII beyond X days.
00:02:36 Ivy Chen: On Hosted we can configure retention windows and we also have dedicated setups where logs and tokens are isolated. We'll include retention options in the doc.

00:03:02 Priya Anand: On scope — for the pilot we want to test: 1) endpoint latency, 2) answer relevance on 5000 SKU Q&A pairs, 3) cost per query estimate. If those are within thresholds we look to expand to a dedicated pool.
00:03:16 Marcus Patel: Good clarity. For that workload, we recommend a quantized model variant to reduce cost while hitting latency. Redwood's runtime supports per-model quantization profiles — sometimes we call them q4/q5 runs, run on A100/NVIDIA T4 depending on dedicated or hosted.
00:03:33 Leah Ortiz: Sorry, q4/q5? Can you explain simply?
00:03:36 Marcus Patel: Yeah — shorthand for 4-bit or 5-bit weight quantization; roughly speaking lower precision reduces memory and can speed throughput but there are small quality tradeoffs. For many retrieval-augmented tasks it's OK. We'll prototype with two model profiles to measure delta.
00:03:53 Tom Bowers: If we start on Hosted, are there model variants we can select? We don't want to be locked into a single model.
00:03:58 Ivy Chen: Hosted gives you the model catalog with pre-curated variants. You can switch models via the API or pin versions. For consistency in the pilot we'll run the same prompt set across both quantized and full-precision variants.

00:04:20 Leah Ortiz: Network architecture: we run in AWS us-west-2; we have strict egress rules. If we use Hosted, what's the setup for VPC peering or private networking?
00:04:29 Marcus Patel: Hosted doesn't do VPC peering by default; it's public API over TLS. For private connectivity, we recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated with inbound peering. Dedicated can be provisioned in your VPC or via private link depending on cloud. We'll sketch that tradeoff: speed vs friction.
00:04:47 Tom Bowers: Private insert will be a later phase. Initial pilot prefers Hosted to reduce ramp time.

00:05:05 Priya Anand: Sounds good. On measuring relevance: do you have an eval harness or recommend evals we can run?
00:05:12 Marcus Patel: Yes, we have a quick eval harness for scoring F1/ROUGE and custom metrics. For retrieval-augmented generation, we'll run both exact-match and human judgment sample. For the pilot, automated metrics on the 5k set plus 100 human-blind evals is the sweet spot.

00:05:35 Ivy Chen: Regarding credits — we can provision an initial $5k trial credit to cover the prototype. That usually covers tens of thousands of tokens depending on model and batching. Does that sound like a good starting point?
00:05:45 Leah Ortiz: Yes. How long do credits last?
00:05:49 Ivy Chen: Typically 90 days. We can extend if we agree on scope.

00:06:05 Tom Bowers: Performance question: our SLAs will likely require tail latency under 600ms for gen. Hosted networks introduce extra hop; do you have data on p95/p99 hosted performance in us-west-2?
00:06:16 Marcus Patel: Average p95 for a medium-size model on Hosted in us-west-2 is ~300-450ms for single-turn generation with small prompt sizes. p99s vary with concurrency; for deterministic SLOs we recommend Dedicated where you control GPU pools. We'll run a benchmark to gather real numbers for your prompt lens.

00:06:42 Leah Ortiz: Great. Can we run a comparison: Hosted with q5 single-node, vs Dedicated small pool, and also a private-later note?
00:06:50 Marcus Patel: Absolutely. For the benchmark run we'll spin up test harness hitting Hosted endpoints with your sample data and, if you want, simulate a small dedicated pool using our lab environment to show delta. We'll include cost estimates per 1k tokens for each.

00:07:12 Priya Anand: Timeline — we're aiming to have a working prototype inside 3 weeks: prototype validation + evaluation, then decision gate. Is that realistic?
00:07:21 Ivy Chen: Yes, with Hosted TTFT that's realistic: day 0 sign-up and API key, day 1 ingest sample prompts, day 2 perf run and tuning. Three weeks gives time for human eval and a small wrap-up.

00:07:36 Leah Ortiz: Who needs to be involved from Redwood for the perf run?
00:07:39 Ivy Chen: Marcus will own the perf plan and run. Sam can help with account setup and credits. I'll handle commercial/credits/paperwork.

00:07:50 Marcus Patel: Quick note on caching: if your product has a high prefix reuse (e.g., same product descriptions), we can enable prefix/KV caching which drastically lowers token costs and improves p95. But we need visibility into query distribution to estimate wins.
00:08:06 Tom Bowers: We'll share logs but they'll be redacted. Is prefix caching compatible with Hosted?
00:08:11 Marcus Patel: On Hosted we have managed caching; for full control and private KV you normally go Dedicated or Private. For the pilot we'll use managed caching to show delta.

00:08:25 Leah Ortiz: Security: SSO is required for our team, and we have an audit requirement to show role-based access.
00:08:31 Ivy Chen: Redwood Console supports SAML SSO and RBAC. We'll attach the setup doc. For audit we can provide trace logs and per-token cost traces.

00:08:46 Priya Anand: Pricing question — if we move to Dedicated after pilot, what's typical minimum commit?
00:08:52 Ivy Chen: Dedicated is usually reserved capacity monthly commits. Small pilots generally move to a burstable or small-reserved pool; typical entry-level months are negotiated but often start at a few K per month. We'll include ballpark numbers.

00:09:10 Leah Ortiz: Are there any enterprise terms around data deletion and audit we should watch for?
00:09:15 Ivy Chen: For Private deployments we can accommodate stricter deletion policies and on-prem. Hosted has configurable retention windows and data deletion workflows; we'll include the legal/security docs for review.

00:09:32 Tom Bowers: One more infra detail: we need to know egress IP ranges for firewall rules.
00:09:37 Sam Rivera: We'll send a link to our published IP ranges and a guide for IP whitelisting. For dedicated/private we'll provide VPC peering or private link details.

00:09:52 Leah Ortiz: Ok. I'd like to nail down the pilot success metrics again: p95 < 600ms, relevance > 80% on auto metrics, and cost estimate under $0.10 per query (ballpark).
00:10:03 Marcus Patel: Noted. We'll measure and produce a short report.

00:10:12 Priya Anand: If results look good, we'd want a follow-up technical deep dive on dedicated sizing and rollout plan.
00:10:18 Ivy Chen: Makes sense. We'll propose that as the next meeting after benchmarks.

-- mid-call more technical exchange --
00:19:02 Marcus Patel: (walks through the benchmark plan) Step 1: ingest 5k SKU Q/A into the harness. Step 2: run 10k requests over a 30-minute window to approximate production concurrency. Step 3: compare q5 vs fp16, measure tokens, cost. Step 4: sample 100 human evals for quality. We'll produce csv with p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens.
00:19:28 Leah Ortiz: For step 2 concurrency, our expected peak is around 8 RPS for early beta — should that shape how you run the test?
00:19:35 Marcus Patel: Yes we'll run at 8 RPS and also a burst test at 25 RPS to understand headroom.
00:19:41 Tom Bowers: How will you simulate retrieval latency? Our retriever adds about 80-120ms on average.
00:19:47 Marcus Patel: We'll add a synthetic 100ms latency to the harness to model retrieval, so end-to-end numbers match your stack.

00:20:05 Leah Ortiz: Any gotchas with prompt engineering? Our prompts have product JSON embedding snippets — sometimes they hit token limits.
00:20:13 Marcus Patel: We'll check token size. If you have embedding-based RAG, use chunking and relevance thresholds. We can also surface token count per request in the report so you can see cost drivers.

00:20:33 Priya Anand: For the trial credits — can we restrict who uses them? We don't want them accidentally used by other teams.
00:20:38 Ivy Chen: Yes, we can scope credits to the account and create API keys with limited quota. Sam will include steps for scoped keys.

00:21:02 Leah Ortiz: Great. Are there any commonly overlooked items customers miss when starting Hosted?
00:21:08 Ivy Chen: Rate limiting — make sure your client uses exponential backoff. Token-level logging and indexing for debug. Also cost visibility — enable token-level dashboards.
00:21:18 Tom Bowers: On the topic of cost visibility, do you provide token-level cost breakdowns per endpoint?
00:21:23 Sam Rivera: Yes, Redwood Console shows per-route and per-model cost and latency breakdowns. You can export for internal billing.

00:21:34 Ivy Chen: Okay let's recap next steps in the call.
00:21:38 Ivy Chen: Action items: I'll provision $5k credits and drop a TTFT quickstart playbook + security pack. Marcus will author the benchmark plan. Leah will provide the sample corpus and SLOs. We'll aim to run bench week of Mar 22.
00:21:54 Leah Ortiz: Sounds good. One note — we'll need the security pack early so our legal can start the review.
00:22:00 Ivy Chen: Understood, will send by tomorrow.

00:22:12 Priya Anand: Anything else before we close?
00:22:15 Marcus Patel: One tiny thing — if you do see hallucinations in the eval, we'll recommend a stricter RAG pipeline and lower generation temperature, which we can tune as part of the pilot.
00:22:26 Leah Ortiz: Yep, we'll watch that.
00:22:30 Tom Bowers: Thanks all — this seems like a good plan.
00:22:34 Ivy Chen: Great, we'll follow up with an email summarizing these items and attach the docs. Thanks everyone.

Post-call auto notes (imperfect):
- Redwood suggests hosted for TTFT; dedicated for guaranteed p99/perf; private for strongest KMS/residency.
- Pilot: 5k SKU Q/A + 10k synthetic requests at 8RPS, synthetic retrieval 100ms, q5 vs fp16, 100 human evals.
- Next meeting: performance deep dive if metrics hit threshold.

End of transcript.
